svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.20 MASONRY AND INSULATING CONCRETE FORM WALLS NOT IN CONTACT WITH THE GROUND
Flashing for Weep Holes in Masonry Veneer

g.text: Flashing to a point 150 mm up the
From a point not less than 5 mm
beyond the outer face of the
Veneer over a wood-frame wall with a sheathing membrane
From a point not less than 5 mm
beyond the outer face of the
Veneer over a wood-frame wall with rigid insulating sheathing

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Flashing beneath weep holes in masonry veneer
over masonry backing walls conforms to the
requirements for cavity walls in Article
Over wood-frame walls, the flashing extends
from a point not less than 5 mm (3/16″) beyond
the outer face of the building element below
the flashing to a point 150 mm (5⅞″) up the
wood-frame wall.
Where the frame wall is sheathed with a
sheathing membrane, a non-wood-based rigid
exterior insulating sheathing or a semi-rigid
insulating sheathing with an integral
sheathing membrane,
the flashing is installed behind the sheathing
membrane or insulating sheathing.
The flashing in Sentence (2) is permitted to
conform to the requirements for concealed
flashing in Table 9.20.13.1.
Drawn: walls cut through, flashing and membrane thickness exaggerated, air space tinted blue, ties not shown. The 150 mm is drawn from the foot of the flashing.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.20.13.6. (page 9-151)
